prompt: A store manager picks a random starting customer, then surveys every $20$th customer who walks in after that. What sampling method is this?
hint: Look for the pattern: a random start, then a fixed SKIP.

hints.text: Look for the pattern: a random start, then a fixed SKIP.
A fixed interval, like every 20th, is the signature of one specific method.
Random start plus a fixed interval is a systematic random sample: choice C.

explanation: The manager chooses a random starting point and then follows a fixed rule: every 20th customer.
That "every $k$th" pattern is a systematic sample.
It is not an SRS, because two customers who arrive back to back can never both be chosen. Choice C.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rule out the others
steps: Stratified would split customers into groups (like morning vs evening shoppers) and sample from each.
Convenience would just grab whoever is nearest the door.
A simple random sample gives EVERY set of customers the same chance, which a fixed skip does not.
